subject: american mink
title: Water Voles Escape Into Burrows. Then a Hunter Arrived That Fits Inside

scenes.text: For water voles, hiding in a burrow always worked. Until this hunter arrived.
Water voles escape danger by diving into the river, or slipping into tunnels in the bank.
Then, in the nineteen twenties, American mink came to British fur farms. They escaped, and bred.
Mink swim well. And a female is small enough to follow a vole right into its burrow.
One mink can wipe out a whole colony. Neither of the vole's escapes works anymore.
From nineteen eighty-nine to ninety-eight, Britain's water voles fell by almost ninety percent.

description:
American mink, brought to Britain for fur farms in the 1920s, escaped and spread along rivers. A female mink is small enough to enter water vole burrows and can wipe out entire colonies.
Between 1989 and 1998 Britain's water vole population fell by almost 90 percent, and mink were a major cause.
Have you ever seen a water vole?
first_comment: In East Anglia, trapping has now cleared mink from thousands of square kilometres, and voles are coming back. Should invasive predators be removed?
